_comment: Repo-level Claude Code hooks. Both entries run `make check-vt-qa`, which derives
BOTH its trigger and its requirement from the diff: it demands a .shux/qa/<scope>/
report only when the change touches VT rendering, and nothing otherwise. ~1s.
This file previously held a Stop hook running `check-progress-active`, which
required every session to append to docs/PROGRESS.md — a shared tail that made two
concurrent branches conflict before they touched code. Issue #123 deleted that, and
with it the only end-of-session enforcement an agent could not simply forget.
These replace it under the rule that issue established: a guard may READ anything,
but must never require you to WRITE to a file someone else is also writing to.
Nothing here writes, and nothing here is shared.

SessionStart runs scripts/ensure-hooks.sh so a fresh checkout — cloud or local — has its git hooks before the first commit. An agent cannot forget to run `make hooks` if it never has to. The CI guard lives in that script, once, because these sessions can run inside GitHub Actions.

PostToolUse runs scripts/check-test-sleeps.sh on every edited file: a test waits for a condition, never for time (docs/testing.md). In crates/*/tests it flags qualified sleep calls and sleep imports on code lines without a statement-level #[expect(clippy::disallowed_methods)]; in any crates/ source or Cargo.toml it flags a waiver of the ban. It says so on stderr; clippy's disallowed-methods is the gate.

hooks.command: INPUT=$(cat); CMD=$(echo "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty'); if echo "$CMD" | grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*git[[:space:]]+push'; then make -C "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" check-vt-qa; fi
hooks.statusMessage: Verifying VT QA evidence before push...
Checking for raw sleeps in test code...
